content: PanoRef coverage optimizer implementation review: algorithm architecture rated 8/10, search mode correctness 7.5/10, complex imported set readiness 4/10. Strengths include deterministic area-proportional sampling, joint-pair mode that genuinely evaluates all legal coarse pairs ranked by bitset union, and a shared coarse-to-fine engine (4,096 coarse, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples). Blockers: (1) imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because obstacle clearance uses per-object AABBs, rejecting any origin inside the enclosing AABB; fix is actual geometry clearance via point-to-triangle distance or shapecast with per-mesh/cluster bounds. (2) Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports—JavaScript objects/arrays/64-bit numbers for 3M triangles require ~144MB minimum packed, actual representation much larger, structured-cloned to worker, plus BVH sorts JS index arrays and raycasts allocate temporary arrays causing GC pressure; fix is compact typed arrays (Float32Array positions/indices/normals, Uint32Array meshRanges/transforms), transferable ArrayBuffers, and flat typed-array BVH or three-mesh-bvh. (3) Geometry extraction still blocks the main thread because extractCoverageScene is called synchronously before worker creation/post; extraction should move into worker or be chunked. (4) UI allows rewriting existing panorama origins via updatePanoReference, which is conceptually wrong—changing metadata doesn't transform the image, ruining alignment; correct workflow preserves existing panoramas, moves capture origins, renders new graybox panoramas, inpaint/stylizes, imports as new panoramas, and associates each with its actual origin. (5) reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + coarse candidates while final combined coverage uses fine sample bank with seed+1, allowing UI to show combined 83%, reachable upper bound 80%, reachable captured 100%; also fixed-first reachable set calculated before arbitrary first origin evaluated, excluding it; fix is common validation sample bank for both final pair coverage and reachable candidate union, and include fixed origin in reachable union for fixed-first. (6) Fixed-first does not enforce minimumOriginSeparation—rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so identical candidate positions survive; add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation. Additional refinements: four-level refinement is not truly iterative (all offsets generated around original seed without updating center after each level); local candidates can float between floors because candidate validation only checks floor existence below candidate and local offsets retain original Y, so on sloped/multilevel sets offsets can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height—fix reproject each offset onto floor under new X/Z with Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters then perform clearance; optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules (optimizer evaluates angle and texel density, but shader blends only by distance when both panoramas visible), so optimized coverage result and visible result don't fully agree—shader should use same approximate quality function and winner-takes-most selection. Testing gaps: no test for one large imported object containing entire room, no 100k+ triangle performance fixture, no reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant test, no fixed-first candidate separation test, no sloped/multilevel floor test, no existing panorama origins immutability test, no candidate generation inside concave imported geometry test; no GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to latest head so test suite not independently enforced in CI. Recent changes: removed stale PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0 constant and projectedConfidence, replaced with projectedQualityAt and dominance mode bias (projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0, projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0); multiOriginInteraction.test.ts updated and passes (36 tests); full test suite passes (42 test files, 371 tests), lint passes (tsc --noEmit), build passes (vite build, 1777 modules transformed). Action items: rebase onto main and resolve PR conflict, add allowed-floor-region mechanism or robust imported-floor component filtering, run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add full 100K+ optimizer integration test (not merely BVH-construction test), then spawn subagent to disprove goal completeness, fix holes, repeat until subagent unable to find holes.

PanoRef coverage optimizer audit and patch cycle: the base capsule records a 42-file/371-test suite passing (typecheck, build, lint) with PR #23 still conflicted remotely and imported-floor filtering still accepting large props (6×6 floor plus disconnected 3×3 tabletop returned all four triangles as legal). A first patch attempt (panoref_evt_001007) added an explicit allowed-floor-region mechanism (CoverageBounds on types.ts, normalize/triangle-intersect helpers in surfaceSampler.ts, floorPointIsAllowed in candidateGenerator.ts, UI toggle + X/Y/Z min-max inputs in CoverageOptimizerPanel.tsx, and a regression test for a large prop top) but failed because README.md lacked the expected connected-component sentence. A shell probe (panoref_evt_001009/001010) and a README grep (panoref_evt_001011/001012) confirmed the current README already describes connected-component filtering, triangle clearance, shared 24,576-sample bank, fixed-first separation, sloped/multilevel reprojection, immutable existing panorama origins, and a 101,250-triangle fixture, plus a docs/ui-revamp-regression-audit.md summary. A second patch attempt (panoref_evt_001013) re-applied the types/surfaceSampler/candidateGenerator changes and succeeded (panoref_evt_001014). A third patch attempt (panoref_evt_001015) applied the CoverageOptimizerPanel UI changes and succeeded (panoref_evt_001016). A fourth patch attempt (panoref_evt_001017) re-applied the test plus a README update and was in progress at snapshot end; the allowed-floor-region mechanism is intended to let users constrain ambiguous large horizontal surfaces (roofs/platforms/prop tops) with explicit world-space bounds instead of relying on geometry-only filtering, complementing connected-component filtering and triangle clearance.

PR #23 on t3code/projector-occlusion is at commit 4153429 ("Lock coverage floor bounds during analysis"), mergeable but with UNSTABLE merge state. The commit locks the coverage floor region toggle and all bound fields during analysis, then unlocks them on completion. Round three adversarial audit found two stale-state holes: editing bounds after a completed run leaves old results and origin-apply actions visible even for origins outside the new region, and changing the primary panorama does not refresh the untouched default region or invalidate a fixed-first result, leaving the region centered on the previous panorama. A follow-up patch centralizes result invalidation for every optimizer input and synchronizes only untouched default bounds to the active capture origin while preserving user-authored bounds. Verification so far includes e2e tests passing on desktop and phone, lint, unit tests (uiFidelity, projectionCoverage, multiOriginInteraction), and a build, all launched but not yet confirmed complete in the snapshot.

PR #23 on t3code/projector-occlusion is at commit 4f4fd39 ("Invalidate stale coverage optimizer results"), mergeable with CLEAN merge state. The commit centralizes result invalidation for every optimizer input and synchronizes only untouched default bounds to the active capture origin while preserving user-authored bounds. Round three adversarial audit found two stale-state holes: editing bounds after a completed run leaves old results and origin-apply actions visible even for origins outside the new region, and changing the primary panorama does not refresh the untouched default region or invalidate a fixed-first result, leaving the region centered on the previous panorama. Round four audit found one remaining cancellation hole: stale extraction failures bypass the analysis-identity check and can overwrite a newer analysis state with `failed`. Verification includes e2e tests passing on desktop and phone, lint, unit tests (uiFidelity, projectionCoverage, multiOriginInteraction), and a build, all launched but not yet confirmed complete in the snapshot. Audit round four is still active against the latest pushed commit with no new finding arrived yet.

PR #23 on t3code/projector-occlusion is at commit 80882e3 ("Ignore stale coverage extraction failures"), mergeable with CLEAN merge state. The commit adds an analysis-identity guard (`if (analysisIdRef.current !== analysisId) return;`) before mutating status in the coverage extraction failure path, closing the round-four cancellation hole where stale extraction failures could overwrite a newer analysis state with `failed`. A regression test verifies both successful and failed coverage extraction guard against stale analysis identity. Verification includes e2e tests passing on desktop and phone, lint, unit tests (uiFidelity, projectionCoverage, multiOriginInteraction), and a build, all launched but not yet confirmed complete in the snapshot. Audit round five is the requested stopping condition: the independent auditor was unable to find any remaining concrete hole. Final verification confirms PR #23 is MERGEABLE/CLEAN with latest Netlify checks passed, local and remote heads match 80882e3 rebased on current origin/main, stale success/worker/extraction-failure paths all enforce analysis identity, bounds/capture changes invalidate results and apply actions correctly, allowed regions constrain extraction/candidate generation/reprojection/refinement through worker transfer, large-tabletop regression passes, the 101,250-triangle test executes both complete optimizer modes, real production-scene benchmark succeeded with no page errors, and typecheck/targeted tests pass on final HEAD.

PR #23 on t3code/projector-occlusion is at commit c1f6c8d ("Update coverage verification count"), mergeable with CLEAN merge state, rebased on current origin/main. The branch preserves the occlusion/coverage implementation and adds explicit world-space allowed-floor regions, connected-component filtering, exact candidate/refinement enforcement, validation, and stale-analysis protection. Final verification confirms 42 test files / 373/373 tests passed, including real WebGL and the full 101,250-triangle optimizer; TypeScript and production build passed; 22 full browser scenarios passed with the final allowed-floor workflow passing on desktop and phone; a real Blender production set (171.2 MB, 191 mesh nodes, 36,788 triangles) ran the full optimizer with 24,576 fine samples in 36.9 seconds and no browser errors; and a build→reference→shots→export smoke produced a valid 33,120,308-byte package. Six adversarial audit rounds were completed; rounds five and six found no remaining concrete holes. The only final change corrects the documented test result from 303/303 to 373/373 and introduces no runtime or configuration change. Netlify deploy-preview checks are SUCCESS, local and remote heads match c1f6c8d, and the temporary local preview process was stopped after browser verification.
